subtitle: Design strategy, customer research and hands-on design for complex software

bio.short: I own design strategy and still do the research and design myself. As Bibel TV's Head of Product Design, I set the direction with product managers and owners, down to prototype code the apps build from. At ChurchDesk, Datameer and Spreadshirt, what I learned from customers changed what got built.
bio.long:
At Bibel TV, a broadcaster moving from linear TV to apps on iOS, Android, web and connected TV, I was Head of Product Design. I set the design direction with product managers and product owners and did the design work myself. In a concept study with 264 app users that I co-designed and analyzed, people found the dark design too gloomy. Their need for brightness and readability made the redesign light-first. The external engineering agency builds from my prototype code. For the redesigned Android Home and detail views, 64% comes verbatim from my prototype (release 6.0, in beta).

At ChurchDesk I owned product management for the main platform and all product design across six European markets. About ten engineers built to my roadmap. A church client asked for funeral booking. Validation with the launch customer, pastors and funeral directors, partly in person, shaped it. I built booking into the platform's calendar instead of a standalone add-on, and it rolled out to every customer.

At Datameer I led UX for five years on data-dense analytics for leading US, Canadian and UK banks and insurers. My research reached hard-to-find enterprise users. At Ninox I learned how small businesses digitize their own workflows, from team leads, owners and the service providers implementing their solutions.
